summary: Tasha Robinson and Pete Volk of Polygon offer a streaming guide for Noirvember, the informal November challenge of watching and comparing noir films. Picks are grouped into classics, next steps, deep cuts, and neo-noirs, each with director, where to watch, and a short review. Each category ends with a list of additional titles.
one_line: Polygon's guide to Noirvember recommends classic, deep-cut, and neo-noir films, with directors, streaming locations, and short reviews.
key_facts: Noirvember is a collective social-media urge to watch and compare noir movies; it has no organizing website, sponsor, fundraising goal, or established rules.
The Maltese Falcon (1941), directed by John Huston, stars Humphrey Bogart as Sam Spade and adapts Dashiell Hammett's 1930 work; it is called probably the most famous noir of all time.
Sunset Boulevard (1950), directed by Billy Wilder, opens with has-been writer Joe Gillis (William Holden) narrating over his floating corpse in a Los Angeles pool, and features Gloria Swanson.
Double Indemnity (1944), directed by Billy Wilder, stars Barbara Stanwyck and Fred MacMurray in an insurance fraud scheme involving the murder of her husband.
M (1931), directed by Fritz Lang, follows a child murderer in Berlin hunted by both police and crime bosses, with a memorable Peter Lorre performance; it is compared to a proto version of The Wire.
Notorious (1946), directed by Alfred Hitchcock, stars Ingrid Bergman as Alicia Huberman, Claude Rains, and Cary Grant, and involves spying on a prominent Nazi figure for the American government.

Detour (1945), directed by Edgar G. Ulmer for Producers Releasing Corporation, runs 66 minutes and features Ann Savage; Ulmer earlier directed The Black Cat and was blacklisted from most studios after an affair with the wife of Carl Laemmle's nephew.
Murder by Contract (1958), directed by Irving Lerner, runs 81 minutes, has an all-guitar score by Perry Botkin, and influenced Martin Scorsese, especially Taxi Driver.
Lured (1947), directed by Douglas Sirk, stars Lucille Ball as taxi dancer Sandra Carpenter, who acts as bait for a serial killer in London.
Blood Simple (1984) was the Coen brothers' first film and Frances McDormand's screen debut; it also features Dan Hedaya.
The Last Seduction (1994), directed by John Dahl, stars Linda Fiorentino as femme fatale protagonist Bridget Gregory and Bill Pullman as her husband Clay.
Brick (2005), directed by Rian Johnson, stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt as a high school kid investigating the death of a girl who jilted him.
Bad Times at the El Royale (2018), directed by Drew Goddard, features Cynthia Erivo, Chris Hemsworth, Jon Hamm, Dakota Johnson, Nick Offerman, and Jeff Bridges at a seedy motel.
Twilight (1998), directed by Robert Benton, is a crime drama with Paul Newman, Susan Sarandon, and Gene Hackman, and is unrelated to the vampire Twilight.
